legend: Epithelioid angiosarcoma composed of sheets of large atypical epithelioid to polygonal cells with ovoid vesicular nuclei, large nucleoli, and relatively abundant cytoplasm.
FISH showing high-level MYC amplification (red signals). The average number of MYC copies per cell is 15.2 and the ratio of MYC to chromosome 8 centromere (D8Z2 locus, green signals) is 8.74.
MYC protein overexpression is evident on immunohistochemistry with an anti-MYC (Y69) monoclonal antibody.
A well-differentiated angiosarcoma involving the dermis.
There is clear nuclear enlargement and hyperchromatism.
In some areas, there is a sieve-like arrangement of vascular channels.
MYC immunohistochemistry is a reliable surrogate marker of MYC amplification and diffusely positive in the majority of radiation-induced secondary angiosarcomas.
An infiltrative neoplasm within dermis is composed of sheets of disorganized poorly formed slit-like vascular spaces.
An infiltrative neoplasm composed of slit-like vascular channels involves the dermis and epidermis, with ulceration.
The tumour cells have scant amphophilic cytoplasm and enlarged nuclei with vesicular chromatin and prominent nucleoli. Epithelioid cytomorphology and papillary formation is seen.
A poorly differentiated infiltrative neoplasm composed of cords and single cells. The tumour cells are epithelioid with enlarged nuclei, vesicular chromatin, and prominent nucleoli.

Post-radiation epithelioid angiosarcoma shows sheets of pleomorphic malignant cells that mimic carcinoma. The vasoformative nature is recognised at the advancing tumour front where anastomosing and slit-like spaces are lined by malignant cells. Immunohistochemistry confirmed endothelial differentiation. There was a history of breast carcinoma with radiation treatment 10 years prior to the development of the current tumour.
